fact_sheet.business_description: S&P Global is a diversified provider of financial information, credit ratings, benchmarks, commodity intelligence, and mobility data [D01]. The company operates through five key segments, earning revenue via subscriptions, transaction-based activity, index licensing, and asset-linked fees [D01].
unit_economics: Capital intensity: Capex of $195 million in FY2025 [D02]
FCF conversion: Reported $5.135 billion defined FCF in FY2025 [D02]
Pricing power: Dependent on market conventions, credibility, and benchmark adoption [D01, D06]
competitive_position: Moat: High switching and coordination costs for established benchmarks and credit ratings [D01, D06]
growth_record_and_outlook: 2026 guidance: 6–8% organic constant-currency revenue growth; EPS $19.40–19.65 [D03]
balance_sheet: Net debt: $11.343 billion as of FY2025 [D02]
Total debt: $13.088 billion (long-term: $12.370 billion; short-term: $718 million) [D02]
management_and_governance: Capital allocation: $6.2 billion returned to shareholders in 2025 ($5.0 billion repurchases, $1.2 billion dividends) [D02]
what_the_market_is_worried_about: AI disruption: Potential for AI to replace research tasks or reduce demand for seat-based software [D01, D05]
Guidance miss: 2026 guidance midpoint of $19.525 missed $20.02 consensus [D03, D05]
Issuance cyclicality: Ratings revenue exposure to capital markets activity [D01, D05]
recent_events: February 10, 2026: Shares fell 9.7% following guidance disappointment [D03, D05]
Mid-2026: Planned Mobility segment separation [D01, D03]
pershing_context: AUM: Core-fund AUM $19.748 billion as of February 9, 2026 [D08]
Holdings: Portfolio includes large-cap franchises like Amazon, Meta, Alphabet, and others [D08]
missing_data: Verified peer forward P/E and FCF yield comparisons for the same date
Product-by-product revenue exposure to AI replacement
Comprehensive historical buyback and ROIC series

simple_predictable_fcf.evidence: The company generates high-margin, recurring subscription and transaction-based revenue through essential financial benchmarks and ratings [D01], with a 50.4% adjusted operating margin and strong FCF conversion [D02].

barriers_to_entry.evidence: S&P Global holds a dominant market position with high switching and coordination costs for its established financial benchmarks and credit ratings [D01, D06].

limited_extrinsic_exposure.evidence: While ratings are sensitive to capital markets activity, the business is diversified across multiple segments, including data, indices, and intelligence, reducing reliance on any single factor [D01].

strong_financial_profile.evidence: The company maintains a manageable debt profile of $13.088 billion total debt against a large market cap, with no mention of a refinancing cliff [D02, D04].

minimal_capital_markets_dependency.evidence: The company generates significant free cash flow, allowing it to return $6.2 billion to shareholders through repurchases and dividends in 2025 [D02].

large_market_cap.evidence: With a market cap of approximately $122.772 billion, it is large and liquid enough for a concentrated position [D04].

attractive_valuation_screen.evidence: Following a 9.7% share price decline due to guidance disappointment, the forward P/E of 20.6x is moderate for a high-quality, dominant franchise [D03, D04, D05].

management_governance.evidence: Management demonstrates disciplined capital allocation, having returned $6.2 billion to shareholders in 2025 [D02].

durable_growth_runway.evidence: The company maintains a steady growth outlook of 6–8% organic revenue growth supported by secular demand for financial data and benchmarks [D03].

gate1.one_line_business_quality_verdict: a highly cash-generative, dominant data and ratings franchise with deep moats and a durable growth profile.

gate2.variant_perception: The market is overly focused on a short-term guidance miss and fears that AI will commoditize S&P Global's research and data offerings [D03, D05]. We believe the company's entrenched market position as an essential financial utility, underpinned by high switching costs and regulatory requirements, makes it largely immune to these concerns, and the recent sell-off provides an attractive entry point for a long-term compounder [D01, D03, D06].
evidence: Shares declined 9.7% on February 10, 2026, due to guidance missing consensus [D03, D05].
Current valuation at 20.6x forward P/E is moderate for a dominant, high-margin franchise with 6-8% organic growth [D03, D04].
Long-term competitive advantage remains intact due to high switching and coordination costs in ratings and benchmarks [D01, D06].
gate2.market_narrative_we_disagree_with: The narrative that AI will significantly disrupt subscription demand and that the 2026 guidance miss signals a structural decline in growth [D03, D05].
what_must_be_true: The competitive moat protecting ratings and benchmark services remains uncompromised by AI tools.
Organic revenue growth continues in the 6–8% range as guided.
Pricing power persists despite potential changes in market data consumption patterns.

gate3.entry_multiple: 20.6x 2026 forward EPS vs historical range for dominant 6-8% growth franchises [D03, D04]

terminal_multiple.why: Reflects a premium for high-moat, free-cash-flow-generative financial utility status despite AI-related sentiment risk.

gate3.downside_case: If AI significantly commoditizes research and issuance volumes remain cyclically depressed, the multiple could contract to 15-17x. Permanent loss is unlikely given the irreplaceable nature of credit ratings and benchmark network effects.
flagged_assumptions: EPS growth beyond 2026 guided range assumed at 8% based on historical compounder performance
Terminal multiple assumption based on comparable high-quality financial data providers

gate4.catalyst_description: We view S&P Global as a high-quality compounder that has been unfairly punished by the market due to a short-term guidance miss and overblown concerns regarding AI disruption [D03, D05]. We expect the share price to re-rate toward a 22x multiple as the company demonstrates the durability of its 6-8% organic growth and the resilience of its moat against AI, effectively fading the current market scare [D03, D06].
levers_or_steps: Continued execution of 6–8% organic revenue growth in the core ratings and indices segments [D03].
Maintenance of high adjusted operating margins at ~50% [D02, D03].
Disciplined capital allocation through consistent share repurchases and dividends, continuing the $6.2 billion return achieved in 2025 [D02].
gate4.why_this_role_fits_the_era: In our 'Pershing Square 3.0' era, we focus on identifying high-quality compounders suffering from temporary dislocations. S&P Global is a dominant, free-cash-flow-generative financial utility. A C0 strategy is appropriate here as the business model is inherently robust; our role is to act as a long-term owner, providing capital stability while the market corrects its mispricing of the firm's growth durability and competitive position.

kill_criteria: Structural decline in operating margins below 45% indicating loss of pricing power.
Organic revenue growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters.
Material loss of market share in credit ratings or indices due to competitive disruption or regulatory changes.
Management shifts from shareholder-friendly capital allocation to debt-funded, low-return acquisitions.
gate5.portfolio_fit: S&P Global fits well within our 3.0 era focus on dominant, cash-generative financial utilities. It complements existing core-fund technology and platform holdings by adding defensive, data-driven financial infrastructure, with no meaningful overlap or factor doubling.
gate5.liquidity_assessment: With a market capitalization of $122.772 billion [D04], the stock is highly liquid, allowing for a position of this size to be established within weeks at well under 15-25% of average daily volume.
gate5.biggest_risk_in_one_sentence: The primary risk is that AI-driven technological shifts commoditize the company's research and data offerings, eroding its competitive moat and pricing power.

valuation.downside_case: Multiple contraction to 15-17x if AI significantly commoditizes research and issuance remains depressed.

The company maintains a strong growth outlook of 6-8% organic revenue growth driven by the secular demand for financial data [D03].

final.memo:
S&P Global is an essential financial infrastructure provider, operating as a dominant, high-margin, and free-cash-flow-generative franchise [D01, D02]. The company’s ratings and indices businesses benefit from high switching and coordination costs, creating a durable competitive moat that is difficult for competitors to replicate [D01, D06]. With a 50.4% adjusted operating margin and significant recurring revenue, the business generates the predictable, high-quality cash flow that defines our standard for a core compounder [D02, D03].

We are able to acquire our stake at a 20.6x forward P/E, a valuation that we believe understates the long-term compounding potential of the firm [D03, D04]. The opportunity arises from a 9.7% share price decline following a short-term guidance miss, which the market has incorrectly extrapolated as a structural impairment to growth [D03, D05]. We view this dislocation as a classic opportunity to buy a great business that is underperforming its potential for fixable or temporary reasons [D03].

Our investment thesis is predicated on the firm’s ability to sustain 6–8% organic revenue growth, supported by the secular demand for financial intelligence [D03]. By maintaining ~50% operating margins and continuing to deploy capital into share repurchases—which totaled $5 billion in 2025—we expect the company to deliver attractive mid-teens annual rates of return [D02, D03]. We anticipate a re-rating toward a 22x terminal multiple as the company demonstrates the resilience of its moat against AI and confirms the durability of its growth profile [D02, D03, D06].

As long-term owners, our role is to support the management team in their continued focus on capital allocation and operational execution [D02]. We identify S&P Global as a high-quality compounder that fits perfectly within our 3.0 era mandate of acquiring dominant utilities during periods of market sentiment weakness. We are initiating a position today with a target of 10% of NAV [D04, D05].
